re_line: 20% China tariff proposed · Shanghai chief Chen Jining purged · Huawei convicted · Senkaku protest
morning_memo: USTR proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies including China at up to *20 percent*, prompting MOFCOM to vow it 'reserves the right to take necessary measures.'
Xi Jinping's anti-graft campaign placed Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, a sitting Politburo member, under investigation, Reuters and Bloomberg report.

A Brooklyn jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 criminal counts including trade-secret theft and sanctions-evasion bank fraud, even as US officials told Congress they found no evidence China's MSS orchestrated Jensen Huang's affair.

key_stat.label: Proposed US Section 301 tariff rate on China
key_stat.context: The highest of 14 new tariffs the USTR proposed Nov 25 under its 'structural excess capacity' probe, versus a 15 percent non-stacked cap for Taiwan, the EU, Japan and South Korea.

prc_government.document: 《服务贸易发展"十五五"规划》(商服贸发〔2026〕212号)
prc_government.detail: MOFCOM and seven other ministries jointly issued the plan Nov 26 setting services-trade development goals through the 15th Five-Year Plan period; a MOFCOM services-trade official briefed press on its contents the same day.
Customs issued Announcement No. 162 of 2026 on Nov 26 further regulating safety supervision requirements for imported and exported cosmetics.

prc_government.action: Launches online platform for supplementary authentication certificates
prc_government.detail: MOFA rolled out an electronic application platform Nov 26 for "electronic supplementary certificates," part of ongoing consular-service digitization.

prc_government.action: Announces December security seminar, naval HADR drill and ASEAN peacekeeping exercise
prc_government.detail: MND said National Defense University will host a Dec 2-14 international security studies seminar; China's navy will hold a Western Pacific Naval Symposium HADR workshop in Nanjing in early December; China and Brunei will co-host a Nov 27-Dec 12 ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus peacekeeping exercise codenamed "Shared Destiny · Peace and Harmony-2026."

prc_government.action: Schedules Rmb100 billion treasury cash deposit auction
prc_government.detail: PBOC said a *Rmb100 billion* two-month central treasury cash deposit auction is set for Dec 1, 2026.

calendar_watch.headline: Taiwan nine-in-one local elections
calendar_watch.detail: Voters choose 22 mayors/magistrates and roughly 11,000 local offices; AP frames it as a mid-term test for President Lai Ching-te.

calendar_watch.headline: China-Brunei co-host ASEAN peacekeeping exercise
calendar_watch.detail: A Nov 27-Dec 12 ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus peacekeeping field exercise codenamed "Shared Destiny · Peace and Harmony-2026" runs in Bandar Seri Begawan.

calendar_watch.headline: PLA hosts international security studies seminar
calendar_watch.detail: China's National Defense University holds a Dec 2-14 seminar on "global security dynamics and regional security cooperation," per the Nov 26 MND briefing.

calendar_watch.headline: Nanjing Massacre National Memorial Day
calendar_watch.detail: China's annual state commemoration of the 1937 Nanjing Massacre (国家公祭日).

calendar_watch.headline: G20 Leaders' Summit, Doral (Miami)
calendar_watch.detail: The US hosts the G20 leaders' summit Dec 14-15; Xi Jinping's attendance has not been confirmed.

overnight_items.headline: Hong Kong marks one year since Wang Fuk Court fire killed 168
overnight_items.body_text: Residents quietly mourned the 168 people killed in the Wang Fuk Court blaze a year ago, the city's deadliest fire since 1980, the New York Times reports. Officials warned against using the disaster to 'sow division' as bereaved families press for accountability.

overnight_items.headline: China launches Shenzhou 24 with two Chinese, one Pakistani astronaut
overnight_items.body_text: China launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft carrying two Chinese astronauts and one Pakistani astronaut, AP reports, extending China-Pakistan space cooperation. **Xi Jinping** hailed the joint mission as the crew heads to the Tiangong space station.

overnight_items.headline: Data from Chinese AI firm MiniMax accessed by unidentified parties
overnight_items.body_text: A researcher told Reuters that data belonging to Chinese AI company MiniMax was accessed by unidentified outside parties, in an exclusive report published Nov 26. The scope of the exposure has not been disclosed.

overnight_items.headline: China's 'female gaze' entertainment boom tests censors' limits
overnight_items.body_text: A thriving Chinese entertainment industry catering to female fantasies, from male dance troupes to paid hiking companions, is testing the limits of Beijing's tolerance, the New York Times reports. The boom reflects shifting consumer-spending patterns among Chinese women.

overnight_items.headline: Huawei teases next-generation AI memory chip to rival Samsung, SK Hynix
overnight_items.body_text: Huawei previewed a next-generation AI memory chip aimed at competing with Samsung and SK Hynix, Bloomberg reports. The move underscores Huawei's push into high-bandwidth memory as US export controls constrain China's access to foreign advanced chips.

overnight_items.headline: EU seeks €50 billion fund for frontier tech to rival US, China
overnight_items.body_text: The European Union is seeking *€50 billion* to fund frontier-technology development aimed at keeping pace with the US and China, Bloomberg reports. The plan reflects growing European concern over falling behind both powers in AI and advanced computing.

us_china.headline: Officials brief Congress: no evidence China directed Huang affair
us_china.body_text: US officials briefed congressional staff that they have found no evidence **China**'s Ministry of State Security directed Huang Le to pursue her relationship with Nvidia CEO **Jensen Huang**, the Wall Street Journal reports. Reuters separately reported that US officials remain divided over the broader spying allegations following Huang's reinstatement as CEO.

us_china.headline: Nvidia halts chip shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia
us_china.body_text: Nvidia told manufacturing partners Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers built with its chips to buyers in four Southeast Asian countries, FT reports, as Washington tightens export controls to prevent Chinese access to AI computing power. It remains unclear whether the halt is temporary.

us_china.headline: How China got access to Nvidia's AI chips despite the rules
us_china.body_text: Reuters examines how advanced Nvidia chips have continued reaching China despite US export restrictions designed to block them. Washington Post separately found that top-tier Nvidia chips remain readily available for sale inside China.

us_china.headline: US chip curbs, distillation crackdown threaten Chinese AI model development
us_china.body_text: Sources tell Reuters that tightening US chip export controls and a crackdown on AI model 'distillation' techniques are threatening the pace of Chinese model development. The constraints add pressure on Chinese labs already contending with reduced access to Nvidia's most advanced processors.

us_china.headline: Second Nvidia executive romance tied to China-linked company surfaces
us_china.body_text: The Wall Street Journal reports on a separate relationship between Nvidia executive Jay Puri and Cenly Chen, an executive at a company with China ties, drawing fresh scrutiny of personal relationships across the chip industry's China-facing supply chain. The report follows the Huang-Huang Le affair that triggered the current congressional inquiry.

us_china.headline: Nuclear-arms control stalls until China 'catches up'
us_china.body_text: The Economist reports US-China-Russia nuclear arms control talks remain stalled, with Washington effectively waiting for China's arsenal to grow before pursuing a trilateral framework. The dynamic complicates any near-term successor to existing bilateral US-Russia arms limits.

china_world.headline: Jensen Huang's comeback reassures Taiwan chip suppliers
china_world.body_text: Taiwanese suppliers found reassurance in **Jensen Huang**'s reinstatement, with veteran tech journalist Owen Lin calling Huang the AI industry's 'central bank' for his role financing so-called neocloud computing firms. Lin said he does not expect Huang's Taiwanese partnerships, including TSMC ties, to change significantly.

china_world.headline: Images fuel debate over whether Japan's Takaichi was snubbed in Shenzhen
china_world.body_text: Photos comparing the welcome given to Japanese Prime Minister **Sanae Takaichi** against other leaders at China's Shenzhen summit have prompted some Japanese officials to allege a snub, the New York Times reports. The dispute adds friction to an already strained Japan-China relationship.

china_world.headline: Suzuki shifts to rare metal-free batteries amid China supply risk
china_world.body_text: Suzuki Motor will produce batteries without rare metals for its kei and minicar lineup, Nikkei reports, seeking to secure affordable batteries without relying on Chinese rare-earth supply chains. The shift reflects broader Japanese industry moves to reduce China dependency after Beijing's rare-earth export controls.

china_world.headline: Chinese consumer advocate Wang Hai stranded in South Korea amid crackdown
china_world.body_text: Prominent Chinese consumer-rights campaigner Wang Hai is stranded in South Korea as a broader crackdown inside China targets consumer advocates, AP reports. His case illustrates tightening space for civil-society campaigners under Beijing's rules.

china_world.headline: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN launch cross-border digital payments talks
china_world.body_text: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN members launched talks on interoperable cross-border digital payment systems, Reuters reports. The initiative aims to streamline regional commerce as Asian economies push deeper financial integration.

china_world.headline: China urges Netherlands to offer 'fair, predictable' climate amid Nexperia dispute
china_world.body_text: **China** urged the Netherlands to provide a fair and predictable business environment amid the ongoing Nexperia dispute, Reuters reports. The standoff over the Dutch-headquartered, China-linked chipmaker remains a flashpoint in European semiconductor supply-chain politics.

top_stories.headline: US proposes new 301 tariffs on China, 13 other trading partners
top_stories.body: USTR proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies including China, the EU, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, with the highest rate of *20 percent* set for China, a senior US official said, per Taipei Times. **MOFCOM** spokesperson He Yadong called the move "typical unilateralism" that "severely violates WTO rules" and said China "reserves the right to take necessary measures." Taiwan's rate is expected to revert to the previously agreed *15 percent* non-stacked cap.

top_stories.headline: Huawei becomes 'indispensable' to China's AI push as Nvidia access shrinks
top_stories.body: As China's access to Nvidia's advanced chips shrinks under US export controls, **Huawei** is becoming increasingly central to Beijing's AI ambitions despite a wide technological gap with its American rival, the New York Times reports. The Trump administration's yearslong campaign to cripple Huawei through export restrictions has instead pushed Chinese AI developers toward the company's domestic alternatives.

top_stories.headline: Huawei found guilty in US trade-secrets, sanctions-evasion trial
top_stories.body: A federal jury in Brooklyn found **Huawei** guilty on 10 of 12 counts, including conspiracy to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks about business in Iran and North Korea, after an 11-week trial, per Taipei Times' report on the verdict. Brooklyn US Attorney Joseph Nocella said the case reflects Huawei's "decades-long pattern of endangering US national security." Huawei was acquitted of racketeering and obstruction charges and says it will review its legal options.

top_stories.headline: China's defence ministry warns Japan to stop 'stirring up' South China Sea disputes
top_stories.body: **MND** spokesperson Chen Xi said Japan should "stop fanning the flames" on the South China Sea issue and warned any attempt to "challenge China's sovereign rights" is "doomed to fail," Reuters reported. Separately, **MOFA** lodged "stern representations" with Japan on Nov 26 over a Japanese vessel's intrusion into waters near the Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands.

top_stories.headline: Taiwan heads into Nov 28 local elections watched closely by Beijing
top_stories.body: Taiwan votes Saturday, Nov 28, in nine-in-one local elections for 22 mayors, magistrates and roughly 11,000 local offices, a vote AP reads as a mid-term test for President **Lai Ching-te**. A Vanderbilt University study cited by the New York Times found pro-Beijing AI-generated personas, including accounts linked to China-based company GoLaxy, inserting pro-unification messaging into non-political social media content ahead of the vote.

top_stories.headline: Xi's anti-graft probe fells Shanghai party chief Chen Jining
top_stories.body: **Xi Jinping**'s government placed Shanghai Communist Party secretary **Chen Jining**, a Politburo member and former Beijing mayor and environment minister, under investigation, Reuters and Bloomberg reported Nov 25. Nikkei Asia said the move "clouds China's leadership reset" ahead of 2027.

also_today.headline: USTR proposes 20% China tariff, keeps Taiwan at 15% cap
also_today.body_text: USTR cited nine 'unreasonable' Taiwan policies while proposing a 20% rate on China and a 15% cap for Taiwan under new Section 301 duties.

also_today.headline: Asian stocks rise on tariff news even as China, HK shares fall
also_today.body_text: Asian markets broadly rose after the US tariff announcement, but China's SSE Composite fell 1.61% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped 2.69% on Nov 26.

also_today.headline: Sinocism previews USTR 301 report, Nvidia fallout, Dutch FM Beijing visit
also_today.body_text: Sinocism's Nov 26 issue covers the USTR 301 report, Nvidia fallout, the Dutch FM's Beijing trip and CICIR's president on new security risks.

also_today.headline: 'Jensanity' sweeps Taiwan and mainland China over Huang's comeback
also_today.body_text: FT: Jensen Huang, 'among the few business leaders to straddle both sides of the Taiwan Strait,' is driving fan enthusiasm in Taiwan and China.

also_today.headline: Zaobao debunks viral link between Lee Hsien Loong remark and Chen Jining's fall
also_today.body_text: Zaobao found social-media claims tying a 2024 Lee Hsien Loong remark on 'China's next generation of leaders' to Chen Jining's purge misread the plural phrasing.

also_today.headline: Li Qiang tells ADB chief China's economy 'withstood pressure' this year
also_today.body_text: Li Qiang told ADB President Masato Kanda China's economy 'withstood pressure and advanced steadily' this year, marking 40 years of China-ADB cooperation.

also_today.headline: China sweeps top three in global science-city rankings
also_today.body_text: China took the top three spots in the Global Research City rankings within the International Science and Technology Innovation Center Index 2026, per MOFCOM.

also_today.headline: China marks 25th WTO anniversary with Geneva dialogue
also_today.body_text: China held a high-level dialogue in Geneva marking 25 years since its Dec 11, 2001 WTO accession, per MOFCOM.

business_economy.headline: Hansoh Pharma strikes $3.3 billion drug deal with Bayer unit
business_economy.body_text: China's Hansoh Pharma signed a licensing deal with a Bayer unit worth nearly *$3.3 billion*, Reuters reports, among the largest China-outbound pharmaceutical agreements this year.

business_economy.headline: Vanke seeks bond extension again as builder distress deepens
business_economy.body_text: Chinese developer Vanke is again seeking a delay on bond repayment, Bloomberg reports, as distress among Chinese builders continues despite earlier state support.

business_economy.headline: Tim Hortons China weighs options including stake sale
business_economy.body_text: Tim Hortons' China operation is weighing strategic options including a stake sale, Bloomberg reports, as the chain reassesses its position in the Chinese market.

business_economy.headline: China-backed Pakistan Exchange prepares to launch stock options
business_economy.body_text: A Pakistan stock exchange backed by Chinese investors is preparing to launch stock options trading, Bloomberg reports, part of continued Chinese capital-markets engagement in Pakistan.

business_economy.headline: Nvidia fallout exposes China's fragility on frontier AI
business_economy.body_text: The lack of US-style capital markets and domestic commercial demand makes it difficult for Beijing to fuel AI innovation on its own, the Financial Times reports following the Nvidia-linked turmoil.

business_economy.headline: Hong Kong launches CMU digital asset platform for bond settlement
business_economy.body_text: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched its CMU Digital Asset Platform on Nov 25, built on distributed-ledger technology, with *over HK$6 trillion* in bond custody as of end-September 2026 and 10 founding member banks including Bank of China (Hong Kong), HSBC and Standard Chartered.

official_line.speaker: He Yadong
official_line.statement: The US Section 301 investigation is a typical act of unilateralism that severely undermines international economic order and gravely violates WTO rules. We firmly oppose this. China urges the US to correct its wrongdoing and return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation. China will closely watch developments, reserves the right to take necessary measures, and will resolutely defend its legitimate rights and interests.
official_line.original_zh: 美方301调查是典型的单边主义行为，严重破坏国际经济秩序，严重违反世贸组织规则，中方对此坚决反对。中方敦促美方纠正错误做法，回到通过对话协商解决问题的正确轨道上来。中方将密切关注事态进展，保留采取必要措施的权利，坚决捍卫自身正当权益。
official_line.context: Statement follows USTR's Nov 25 proposal of Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies, with the highest rate of 20 percent aimed at China.

official_line.speaker: TAO spokesperson
official_line.statement: Per TAO: the Trump-Xi summit provided 'new strategic guidance' for US-China relations, and China hopes Washington will put into practice its stated non-support for 'Taiwan independence' and avoid letting the Taiwan question disrupt the broader picture of ties.
official_line.original_zh: 国台办发言人表示：中美元首会晤作出两国关系新战略指引，希望美方将不支持"台独"落到实处，避免台湾问题干扰中美关系大局
official_line.context: Comment follows recent Trump-Xi engagement referenced in Chinese state media coverage of cross-strait and bilateral ties.

official_line.speaker: MOFA spokesperson
official_line.statement: Per MOFA: the Japanese vessel's illegal intrusion into Diaoyu Islands waters seriously violated China's sovereignty and undermined stability there; China has lodged stern representations with Tokyo.
official_line.original_zh: 日本船只非法侵闯钓鱼岛领海挑衅滋事，外交部：严重侵犯中国主权，破坏钓鱼岛局势稳定，中方已向日方提出严正交涉
official_line.context: A Japanese vessel entered waters near the Senkaku/Diaoyu Islands on Nov 26, prompting the formal protest.

official_line.speaker: Chen Xi
official_line.statement: We demand that Japan stop fanning the flames and stirring up trouble on the South China Sea issue; any attempt to challenge China's sovereign rights and interests or undermine regional peace and stability is doomed to fail.
official_line.original_zh: 我们要求日方停止在南海问题上拱火滋事，任何试图挑战中国主权权益、破坏地区和平稳定的图谋都注定失败。
official_line.context: Remarks made at the Nov 26 MND monthly press briefing amid Japan-China friction over the South China Sea and East China Sea.

official_line.speaker: Chen Xi
official_line.statement: We urge Japan to provide effective information on burial sites as soon as possible, increase human resource input, comprehensively speed up the disposal of its abandoned chemical weapons, and completely eliminate this poison at an early date, returning a clean land to the Chinese people.
official_line.original_zh: 我们督促日方尽快提供有效埋藏线索信息，加大人力资源投入，全面加快日遗化武处置进程，早日彻底清除日遗化武毒害，还中国人民以净土。
official_line.context: Comment made at the same Nov 26 briefing, timed to China's release of the "Huan Wo Jing Tu" documentary on Japan's abandoned WWII-era chemical weapons.

social_statements.handle_context: US Attorney for the Eastern District of New York
social_statements.quote_text: Few crimes are as serious as Huawei's decades-long pattern of endangering US national security, violating the sanctity of US commerce, and impeding the enforcement of US laws.
social_statements.analyst_note: Statement followed a Brooklyn federal jury's guilty verdict on 10 of 12 counts against Huawei after an 11-week trial.

social_statements.quote_text: It's hard not to have profoundly mixed emotions from the verdict we just heard.
social_statements.analyst_note: Huawei was acquitted of RICO racketeering and obstruction charges but convicted on 10 of 12 counts including trade-secret theft and sanctions-related bank fraud.

personnel_changes.position: Shanghai CCP Party Secretary / Politburo member
personnel_changes.name: Chen Jining
personnel_changes.detail: Xi Jinping's government placed Chen Jining, a Politburo member and former Beijing mayor and environment minister, under investigation, Reuters and Bloomberg reported Nov 25. Jamestown Foundation analysis said the move ends the "Tsinghua clique's" hold on a traditional path to the top leadership.
